# sonrai_control_reset (Resource)

Rolls every control under a root scope back to staged.

**This is destructive and organization-wide.** It returns applied controls to staged, stages quarantined identities for removal, and re-stages JIT permission sets and levels for re-creation. It does not distinguish between controls Terraform manages and controls created from the console or by automation.

The reset cannot finish while the firewall's CloudFormation stack still exists: the transaction hands off to the cloud and waits for the stack to go. Order the two with `depends_on`, so one apply deletes the stack and then runs the reset.

```hcl
resource "sonrai_control_reset" "firewall" {
  count = var.reset ? 1 : 0

  root_scope = var.root_scope
  confirm    = "aws/r-abcd"

  depends_on = [aws_cloudformation_stack.firewall]
}
```

Terraform state stays accurate afterwards. The controls remain staged and report the same status, so the next plan shows no changes, and clearing `reset` deploys them again.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Arming this clears every control under the root scope, including controls
# this configuration did not create. Keep it behind a variable that defaults to
# false, and write confirm out by hand so one flipped flag is never enough.
variable "reset" {
  description = "Tear the deployment down and return every control to staged."
  type        = bool
  default     = false
}

# The reset transaction waits for the CloudFormation stack to be deleted before
# doing the rest of its work, so depends_on puts both into one apply: the stack
# goes, then the reset runs and this resource waits for it to complete.
resource "sonrai_control_reset" "firewall" {
  count = var.reset ? 1 : 0

  root_scope = "aws/r-abcd"
  confirm    = "aws/r-abcd"

  depends_on = [aws_cloudformation_stack.firewall]
}

output "reset" {
  value = var.reset ? {
    transaction_id = one(sonrai_control_reset.firewall[*].transaction_id)
    status         = one(sonrai_control_reset.firewall[*].status)
  } : null
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `confirm` (String) Must repeat `root_scope` exactly, and is checked when the plan is built rather than when it is applied. Without this an organization's controls would be cleared by a single variable. Write the scope out by hand: pointing both attributes at the same variable makes the check satisfy itself.
- `root_scope` (String) Cloud organization root scope to reset, for example `aws/r-abcd`.

### Optional

- `wait` (Boolean) Whether to wait for the reset to complete before the apply returns. Defaults to true. Setting it false returns as soon as the transaction starts, leaving the reset to finish unobserved.
- `wait_timeout` (String) How long to wait, as a Go duration such as `2h`. Defaults to `2h`, and cannot exceed `24h`, the point at which a transaction expires.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Transaction id of this reset.
- `status` (String) Transaction status reported by the platform.
- `status_message` (String) Human-readable detail accompanying the status.
- `transaction_id` (String) Transaction id returned by the platform.
